column2: With her coach's help, she managed to surmount every obstacle on the course.
column3: 在教練的幫助下，她設法克服了賽道上的每一個障礙。
column5: sur 在上面 + mount 爬：一步步爬過障礙

column2: The cost of digging the tunnel proved an insurmountable barrier to the project.
column3: 挖隧道的成本成了這項計畫無法克服的障礙。
column5: in 不 + surmount 爬過 + able：爬不過去的
column8: 無法克服的；難以踰越的

column2: Temperate forests lose their leaves in autumn and rest through cool winters.
column3: 溫帶森林在秋天落葉，並在涼爽的冬季休息。
column5: temper 調節：氣溫調得剛剛好，不極端

column2: Temperance in eating and drinking kept the old sailor healthy into his nineties.
column3: 飲食上的節制讓這位老水手到九十多歲仍然健康。
column5: temper 調節 + ance：把自己調到不過量

column2: Villagers venerate the ancient oak as a living symbol of their ancestors.
column3: 村民崇敬這棵古老的橡樹，視它為祖先的活象徵。
column5: 想像對年長智者恭敬鞠躬，滿心景仰

column2: The old statue was an object of veneration for generations of pilgrims.
column3: 這座古老的雕像是世世代代朝聖者崇敬的對象。
column5: venerate 崇敬 + tion：心中充滿敬意的狀態

column2: New evidence helped vindicate the engineer who had warned about the cracks.
column3: 新證據證明了那位曾警告裂縫問題的工程師是對的。
column4: vindicate a claim (證明主張正確)
column5: 想像法官敲槌，宣布「你是清白的、你是對的」

column2: The test results brought vindication to the scientist whose theory had been mocked.
column3: 測試結果為那位理論曾被嘲笑的科學家平反。
column5: vindicate 證明正確 + tion：名詞就是平反的結果

column2: The speaker opened her talk with a funny anecdote about her first day at school.
column3: 講者以一則關於她上學第一天的有趣軼事開場。
column5: an + ec + dote：一段沒寫進正史的小故事

column2: Anecdotal stories about miracle cures are not enough to prove a drug works.
column3: 關於神奇療法的軼事傳聞，不足以證明藥物有效。
column5: anecdote 小故事 + al：只有故事，沒有系統數據

column2: The monk lived in an austere room furnished with only a mat and a lamp.
column3: 那位僧人住在只有一張蓆子和一盞燈的簡樸房間裡。
column5: 想像空蕩蕩、沒有裝飾、冷冷清清的房間

column2: Years of austerity forced the town to close its library and cut bus routes.
column3: 多年的緊縮政策迫使小鎮關閉圖書館並減少公車路線。
column5: austere 嚴苛簡樸 + ity：勒緊褲帶過日子

column2: The belligerent neighbor shouted at anyone who parked near his gate.
column3: 那位好鬥的鄰居對任何把車停在他門口附近的人大吼。
column5: belli 戰爭（像 rebellion 反叛）：一副要開戰的樣子

column2: His belligerence in meetings made colleagues avoid any open debate.
column3: 他在會議中的好鬥態度，讓同事們避免任何公開辯論。
column5: belligerent 好戰的 + ce：名詞就是那股好鬥勁

column2: A monk wrote a chronicle that recorded every harvest and flood for fifty years.
column3: 一位僧人寫了一部編年史，記錄了五十年間每一次豐收與水災。
column5: chron 時間（像 chronic 長期的）：照時間順序記下來

column2: The essay lacked coherence because its paragraphs jumped from topic to topic.
column3: 這篇文章缺乏連貫性，因為各段落在不同主題間跳來跳去。
column5: co 一起 + her 黏（像 adhere 黏貼）：黏在一起不散

column2: Complacency after early success cost the team the championship.
column3: 早期成功之後的自滿，讓球隊丟掉了冠軍。
column5: com 完全 + plac 滿意（像 please）：自己滿意就不再進步

column2: The champion grew complacent and stopped practicing, so a younger rival beat him.
column3: 那位冠軍變得自滿而停止練習，結果被較年輕的對手擊敗。
column5: com 完全 + plac 滿意：滿意到躺平不想努力

column2: The strange results continued to confound researchers for years.
column3: 這些奇怪的結果多年來一直讓研究人員困惑不已。
column5: con 一起 + found 倒：全部攪在一起，頭腦打結

column2: Her bright red coat was conspicuous against the gray winter crowd.
column3: 她鮮紅的外套在灰撲撲的冬日人群中格外顯眼。
column5: con 全部 + spic 看（像 spectator 觀眾）：一眼就被看到

column2: The cart was the only conveyance available to carry the harvest to market.
column3: 那輛推車是唯一可以把收成運到市集的運輸工具。
column5: convey 運送 + ance：負責運送的東西

column2: He left a cryptic note on the desk that nobody could decode.
column3: 他在桌上留下一張沒人能破解的神祕字條。
column5: crypt 地下密室：藏在暗處，看不懂意思

column2: Leaders from every party gathered to denounce the attack and demand justice.
column3: 各黨派的領袖齊聚，公開譴責這起攻擊並要求正義。
column4: denounce a policy (公開譴責政策)
column5: de 向下 + nounce 說：大聲說出它的不對

column2: The newspaper's fierce denunciation of the plan stirred public protest.
column3: 報紙對該計畫的嚴厲譴責引發了民眾抗議。
column5: denounce 譴責 + tion：名詞就是譴責的聲明

column2: The painting's depiction of a stormy harbor feels almost alive.
column3: 這幅畫對暴風雨港口的描繪幾乎栩栩如生。
column4: depiction of life (對生活的描繪)
column5: de + pict 畫（像 picture 圖畫）：畫出來的樣子

column2: Critics would deride the inventor's flying machine as a foolish toy.
column3: 評論家會嘲笑這位發明家的飛行器只是愚蠢的玩具。
column4: deride someone's efforts (嘲笑某人的努力)
column5: de 向下 + rid 笑（像 ridiculous 可笑的）：笑到對方抬不起頭

column2: The crowd met his boast with laughter and derision.
column3: 群眾以笑聲和嘲弄回應他的自誇。
column5: deride 嘲笑 + sion：名詞就是嘲弄的態度

column2: The desolate island had no trees, no people, and only wind.
column3: 那座荒涼的島上沒有樹，沒有人，只有風。
column5: de 完全 + sol 單獨（像 solo）：只剩孤零零一片

column2: A feeling of desolation settled over the empty village after the flood.
column3: 洪水過後，一股淒涼的感覺籠罩著空蕩蕩的村莊。
column5: desolate 荒涼 + tion：名詞就是那片孤寂荒蕪

column2: The devious clerk took an indirect route to hide the mistake.
column3: 那位狡詐的店員繞了一條迂迴的路來掩蓋錯誤。
column5: de 離開 + via 路：不走正路，專走歪路

column2: Dilute the juice with water so the little ones don't get too much sugar.
column3: 把果汁加水稀釋，小朋友就不會攝取太多糖。
column5: di 分開 + lute 洗：加水沖淡，味道變弱

column2: Dilution of the cleaner made it safer to use on delicate surfaces.
column3: 清潔劑經過稀釋後，用在脆弱的表面上更安全。
column4: dilution of a solution (溶液稀釋)
column5: dilute 稀釋 + tion：名詞就是被沖淡的過程

column2: The diminution of the glacier over fifty years alarmed local scientists.
column3: 冰河五十年間的縮減令當地科學家警覺。
column5: dimin 像 minus 減：一直減少變小

column2: To their dismay, a sudden storm canceled the picnic they had planned for weeks.
column3: 令他們沮喪的是，一場突來的暴風雨取消了他們籌劃數週的野餐。
column5: dis 失去 + may 力量：嚇到全身沒力氣

column2: The captain will dispatch a rescue boat as soon as the storm calms.
column3: 風暴一平息，船長就會立刻派出救援船。
column5: 想像快遞員一聲令下，馬上被派出去

column2: A disputatious uncle turned every family dinner into a lively argument.
column3: 一位好爭辯的叔叔，把每場家庭聚餐都變成熱烈的爭論。
column5: dispute 爭論 + atious：愛挑起爭論的人

column2: The eccentric inventor wore a cape and talked to his tomato plants.
column3: 那位古怪的發明家披著斗篷，還會對他的番茄苗說話。
column5: ex 外 + centric 中心：偏離中心、不走尋常路的人

column2: Her only eccentricity was serving every guest soup in a teacup.
column3: 她唯一的怪癖，就是用茶杯為每位客人盛湯。
column5: eccentric 古怪 + ity：名詞就是那個小怪癖

column2: The report exposed an egregious error that cost the company millions.
column3: 這份報告揭露了一個讓公司損失數百萬的極其離譜的錯誤。
column5: e 外 + greg 群（像 gregarious 合群的）：離群到過分的壞

column2: The elusive snow leopard is rarely seen, even by those who study it.
column3: 難以捉摸的雪豹連研究牠的人也很少見到。
column5: 想像抓泥鰍，一伸手就滑走了，抓不住
